title: Attempt to serve Storybook through architecture-studio's own origin via Next.js rewrites, to fix the cross-origin postMessage failure inside the /storybook iframe
objective: Owner-directed: confirmed the /storybook iframe's Actions panel silently fails (SecurityError inside Storybook's own Channel.emit -> PostMessageTransport.send) because apps/architecture-studio (127.0.0.1:4511) and the standalone Storybook dev server (localhost:6006) are different origins to the browser -- opening Storybook directly at :6006 works correctly (owner confirmed: Actions panel showed the real onClick event object). Owner explicitly asked to attempt a same-origin fix via Next.js rewrites() proxying a path under architecture-studio's own origin to the Storybook dev server, after being warned (with external evidence: multiple long-standing storybookjs/storybook GitHub discussions/issues, e.g. #25858, #22280, #1291, describing subpath/reverse-proxy deployment as unreliable/incompletely supported, particularly for the manager UI bundle which is separate from the Vite-built preview our own viteFinal hook can already influence) that this is real, externally-documented risky territory, not a routine config change. Attempt it, verify concretely (HMR still works, manager assets load, Controls/Actions still function through the proxied path), and be honest in the task record and to the owner if it only partially works or needs to be reverted.
validations: DONE (attempt 1 -- worked): added a Next.js rewrite proxying /storybook-app/:path* to http://localhost:6006/:path*, pointed the /storybook iframe's src at the same-origin /storybook-app path instead of the raw http://localhost:6006 URL. Confirmed manager HTML, index.json, and manager runtime assets all serve correctly through this prefix.

DONE (attempt 2 -- real bug found and fixed): a story module's actual component import uses a Vite-internal ROOT-absolute path (`/@fs/<absolute path>`, confirmed by fetching the story module directly), which an ES module resolves against the origin root, not the current page's path -- this bypassed the /storybook-app/* prefix entirely and 404d, breaking the story's real component import (not just cosmetic). Root-caused by direct HTTP inspection, not guessed.

DONE (attempt 3 -- escalating whack-a-mole, then a robust fix): enumerating individual Vite root paths one at a time (@fs, @vite, @id, node_modules) kept surfacing more (vite-inject-mocker-entry.js, .storybook/preview.ts, with no reason to expect that list was complete) -- exactly the unbounded-edge-case pattern the earlier external research (storybookjs/storybook discussions #25858/#22280, issue #1291) warned about. Replaced the growing allowlist with a single Next.js `fallback`-phase rewrite (lowest-priority rewrite category: only applies once neither a real page/route nor a public file matched) that proxies ANY otherwise-unmatched request to Storybook's own root. This can never shadow this app's own routes and requires no further enumeration -- verified directly against every path found broken across all three attempts (@fs, sb-manager, vite-inject-mocker-entry.js, .storybook/preview.ts, index.json, iframe.html), all now 200.

DONE (real regression found, then reverted): the fallback rule alone still needed either a trailing slash on /storybook-app or some other fix for Storybook's own relative asset paths (./sb-manager/runtime.js) to resolve correctly, since Next's default trailingSlash:false 308-redirects /storybook-app/ -> /storybook-app, breaking relative resolution. Tried global `trailingSlash: true` -- concretely confirmed this 308-redirects /lab, /storybook, and (seriously) the real `/api/mcp` POST endpoint that apps/architecture-studio's own agents surface depends on, a genuine regression to already-working functionality (not just a theoretical risk -- reproduced with a real POST request via curl). Reverted trailingSlash entirely once realized the `fallback` rewrite already solves the same underlying problem for free: any relative asset request that lands on the origin root (because of the missing trailing slash) is exactly the kind of otherwise-unmatched request the fallback rule already proxies to Storybook -- no global config change needed at all.

DONE: full re-verification after the revert -- root, /lab, /agents, /storybook, and a real POST to /api/mcp (with the same JSON-RPC initialize payload the real MCP client sends) all return 200 again; the entire Storybook proxy chain (/storybook-app, sb-manager assets, vite-inject-mocker-entry.js, .storybook/preview.ts, index.json, iframe.html, @fs component import, the story module's actual transformed content) also all return 200 through the same, now-simpler config. architecture-studio's own tsc --noEmit clean. Both dev servers (Next.js at :4511, Storybook at :6006) confirmed running and the Storybook story index (7 entries) fetchable through the full proxy chain.

NOT DONE (accepted limitation, needs the owner's own browser check): whether the original SecurityError (Channel.emit -> PostMessageTransport.send cross-origin failure) is actually gone now that the whole frame nesting chain is same-origin from the browser's perspective was reasoned from the HTTP-level evidence (no cross-origin boundary remains anywhere in the chain) but not independently confirmed by watching a real browser's Actions panel through the /storybook iframe -- no browser-automation tool is available this session. Vite's HMR WebSocket is also NOT proxied (Next.js rewrites only handle plain HTTP) -- editing a story still needs scripts/generate-stories.mjs plus a manual refresh through the iframe, same as before this task.
artifacts: apps/architecture-studio/next.config.mjs (fallback-based same-origin Storybook proxy; no global config changes)
apps/architecture-studio/src/app/storybook/storybook-client.tsx (iframe src changed from http://localhost:6006 to the same-origin /storybook-app path)
risks: This remains dev-server-specific plumbing (rewrites proxying to a hardcoded http://localhost:6006) -- if the Storybook port ever changes, or if this ever needs to work against a production/built Storybook rather than its dev server, this config would need revisiting; out of scope for this task.

The fallback rewrite proxies literally any request architecture-studio itself doesn't otherwise claim to the Storybook dev server -- safe today (Storybook's dev server 404s cleanly for anything it doesn't recognize either), but worth remembering if a future unrelated 404 in this app turns out to be silently swallowed by this fallback instead of surfacing as a real 404 from this app.

Confirmed empirically (not assumed) that the earlier evidence-based warning about Storybook subpath/proxy fragility was well-founded -- this took three escalating fix attempts, one of which (trailingSlash: true) produced a real regression to a previously-working feature (/api/mcp) that was caught before being left in place, not merely anticipated.
